# Part VI: Modelling and Risk Scoring {.unnumbered}

Some audit questions are about what to expect. How much should this unit have spent? Which claims are most likely to be wrong? This part covers models that learn from data, and from past audit results, to answer them.

Linear regression gives expected values to compare with actual ones. Logistic regression, decision trees and random forests learn from past findings and score new cases by risk. Data envelopment analysis compares the efficiency of units like health centres and bus depots.

These methods rank and select. They do not prove. Every chapter shows how to turn their output into a list of cases to examine, and how to explain why each case was chosen.
